title: New Caledonia
capsule: New Caledonia (French: Nouvelle-Caledonie) is a Melanesian archipelago in the southwestern Pacific, charted and named by Captain James Cook in 1774 and formally annexed for Napoleon III's France by Admiral Febvrier Despointes on 24 September 1853. In the late 1850s it was a sparsely held new colonial possession rather than a penal settlement: Captain Tardy de Montravel had founded the capital, Port-de-France (renamed Noumea in 1866), on 25 June 1854, and only a handful of free settlers had taken up land along the western coast while the French consolidated administrative control over the indigenous Kanak population. Large-scale convict transportation did not begin until 1864, after this period, ultimately bringing some 22,000 prisoners through 1897.
